fixed_by: issue #102 — `joinUnits` in `RubyCore/Builtins/Support.lean` and the `__join_collect` twin in `prelude/prelude.rb`
note: `ary_join` inserts a separator around each element as a unit and joins a nested Array with the same separator, so an empty nested Array is a unit that renders "" and keeps both boundaries: `[[], 1].join("-")` is `"-1"`, `[1, [], 2].join("-")` is `"1--2"`. The model flattened the nesting into one list of rendered parts first (`flattenAll` then `String.intercalate`), so every empty nested Array removed a separator. Both implementations carried the defect: the native `joinImpl` and the prelude twin `__join_slow`, which dispatch picks when an element answers `to_ary` or when some element's `to_s` is overridden, so the case pins both (the `to_ary` and `to_s` groups below). `nil` and the empty separator are controls: `nil` renders "" without consulting `NilClass#to_s` (which `toS` already agrees with), and an empty separator hides the boundary either way.
